title: Zumi episode manifest
description: manifest.json at the root of a .zumi file (a zip). Assets are grouped per panel under panels/<panelId>/ and per episode under episode/, and referenced by relative path from the root. Version 1.1.0, 2026-11-15 (1.0.0: 2026-10-17). This schema is the source of truth of the format; README.md holds the conventions it cannot state. See docs/architecture/decisions.md sections 2 and 3.

formatVersion.description: The version of this schema the file was written to (the last path part of $id). A reader accepts any 1.x and ignores fields it does not know; a file may not name a version newer than the schema it is checked against

generator.description: Tool and version that packed this file, e.g. zumi-pipeline 0.3.1

style.description: Snapshot of the series style definition used for this episode

music.description: Instrumental tracks of this episode. With episode.score (every pipeline-made file) the score's envelope alone says which track sounds when. Without it (hand-made files) the first track starts with panel 0 unless panel 0 names a cue, and panels switch tracks with musicCue

durationHint.description: Seconds, the last panel's endTime when the pipeline precomputed the timeline, else the sum of panel durations; informational

settings.description: The places the episode is drawn in (pipeline step 10): a frame names its setting in panels[].frames[].setting. Places, props and music hang on them

places.description: Settings' surroundings shown through the reader's walls (pipeline step 10c): each place is a wide painted view lifted to two meshes around the seat, and the timeline says which place shows when. A reader fades the open place out over `fade` seconds, then the next one in; no place outside the timeline

fade.description: Seconds of each half of a swap

timeline.description: In time order on the episode clock: seconds from the episode start

score.description: The music as the pipeline resolved it: per-track gain envelopes on the episode clock, and the reviewer's spans as data. When present a reader follows the envelopes and ignores musicCue and music[].gain. The envelope is final: it already holds each role's level, the ducking under every voiced line, every entrance, crossfade and fade, and the opening and closing of the place the track is heard through. A reader multiplies a track by its gain at the clock's time and does nothing else to its level: it must not duck under voices again. Playback position: a track is audible while its gain is above 0.001; its origin at clock time t is the time of the last knot at or before t whose gain is at most 0.001 and whose next knot's gain is above 0.001 (the start of the audible span t lies in), or its first knot's time when there is none; at t it plays its file at ((t - origin) modulo music[].duration) seconds, the whole file looping (the pipeline writes the loop body as the file and no loopStart/loopEnd). So a seek lands where straight play would be, and a track that fell silent starts from its beginning when it enters again

envelope.description: music[].id -> knots [[seconds, gain], ...] in time order; gain 0..1 is the track's linear level, linear between knots, 0 before the first and after the last. A track with no knots never sounds

placement.description: How the music sits in the room over time, by role (music is made for the open place and heard through its portal): point = from one point inside the place (music heard in the scene), wide = spread across the open walls (lead, underscore: in the reference its two channels from the front of the left and right walls). In time order, seconds on the episode clock; outside every entry, wide

yaw.description: point only: the direction of the point from the seat, in the open place's frame as placeLight.key.yaw (degrees from straight ahead, positive to the right). The reference puts the point 2 m beyond the wall along it. The pipeline writes 0: nothing measures where the players stand

pitch.description: point only: degrees above the horizon

from.description: The first bubble or frame of the span: p<panel>/b<bubble> or p<panel>/f<frame>

cast.description: The characters of this episode: everyone a character card is (a node's extras.cast, a bubble's speakerId), speaking or not. Snapshot of the series cast at publish time. A member without a voice does not speak in this episode

description.description: The text the voice was designed from

layout.description: How panels are presented. Absent means carousel.

mode.description: scroll: one tall strip reassembled from the panels in order, stepped beat by beat; carousel: one card per panel

width.description: Strip width in source pixels (WEBTOON 800, Naver 700). Required for scroll

height.description: Total strip height in source pixels, including gutters

background.description: Gutter and margin colour measured from the strip edges

episodeImagePath.description: Episode-level image: cover.png, thumbnail.png, or refs/<name>

panelImagePath.description: Inside the panel's own folder: layers/<layerId>.png, panorama.jpg, depth/<layerId>.png

voicePath.description: panels/<panelId>/voice/<bubbleId>.wav: RIFF WAVE, PCM, 24 kHz, mono, 16-bit, a 44-byte header and nothing after the samples. PCM because Unity cannot decode MP3 or Ogg from memory; a reader copies the samples into a clip

ambiencePath.description: Reserved: one loop per panel. The pipeline writes none

episodeAudioPath.description: The pipeline writes WAV (PCM): a loop body that closes without a seam, which a lossy codec's padding would break

gain.description: Linear level of the track in a file without episode.score, where the reader also ducks the music under voices itself. With a score it is 1 and unused: the envelope is the level, ducking included

loopStart.description: Seconds; loop region start for seamless loops (optional; hand-made files)

loopEnd.description: Seconds; loop region end (optional; hand-made files)

setting.description: episode.settings[].id the track belongs to (the tracks of one setting share tempo, key and instruments)

duration.description: Seconds of audio in the file: the modulus of the playback position (episode.score)

musicCue.description: Hand-made files only (ignored when episode.score is present; the pipeline writes none). Placed on a panel: when the panel appears, switch to this track with the given transition.

track.description: episode.music[].id, or 'none' to fade music out

transition.description: crossfade: equal-power overlap; fadeOutIn: silence gap between tracks; cut: immediate (use only on hard scene breaks)

startAt.description: Seconds into the new track to start from

at.description: Seconds after the panel appears before the cue fires (a cue on a frame inside the panel)

place.description: One place: two meshes in one frame, how far it is, its light and its props. The frame (glTF's, right-handed): the origin is the seat's eye, +y up, the view's centre straight ahead down -z, +x to the right. Both meshes are unlit (KHR_materials_unlit: the painting is already lit) and in metres as the depth model estimated them, not the room's. A reader shows a place so: (1) the origin at the eye of the seat, the one fixed point the place's directions are measured from; (2) -z turned, about +y, to the key wall: the horizontal direction from the seat to the wall the place is shown on, perpendicular to that wall; (3) the place is seen through one window only: a rectangle on the key wall (the nearest wall behind the panel; with no scanned room a virtual wall 2 m ahead of the seat) centred on the panel's direction from the seat, of a default angular size seen from the seat (100 degrees across, 56 up, about the eye's level), its lower edge never below 0.2 m above the floor, cut to the wall's extent when the wall is smaller, fading out over a soft edge on all four sides; never through the side walls, the ceiling or the floor (since 2026-11-16; on 2026-11-15 a warp of the place's directions fitted it to the whole room and read as stretched); (4) both meshes scaled by one factor s about the origin, every point kept in its own direction: s is the weighted 95th percentile, over the front mesh's vertices seen through the window, of (the distance from the eye to the key wall along the vertex's direction + 0.25 m) / (the vertex's distance from the origin), each weighted by how much of it shows, so 95 % of what the reader sees lies beyond the wall; every back vertex nearer than (the wall's distance along its ray + 0.1 m) / s is pushed out along its ray to that distance; (5) what still falls inside the room is clipped. In its own directions the place spans hDeg / 2 to either side of -z and vDeg / 2 above and below the horizon, fading out over the last degrees

front.description: The view as a mesh, cut at depth edges

back.description: The surface behind the front's near objects, a little farther, never cut; shown through the front's gaps

hDeg.description: Degrees the view spans across, centred straight ahead

vDeg.description: Degrees it spans up and down, centred on the horizon

nearM.description: The 5th percentile of the distance from the eye over the view, in the meshes' units: 95 % of the place is farther

medianM.description: The median distance from the eye over the view, in the meshes' units

farM.description: The 95th percentile; the sky, where the view has one, is farther still

props.description: Objects of the place that stand in the reader's room while the place is open (pipeline step 10d). No positions: the reader puts each on a real surface of the kind it names, near the open wall, and fades it with the place

prop.description: One prop and its model's conventions. The model is a glTF binary with one mesh, as the lifting model (TRELLIS) leaves it: +y up; centred on the origin inside a unit cube (its longest side about 1, see bounds), so the origin is the middle of the model, not its base; the side the place's view shows faces +z (as the model lifts a picture; not checked per prop, a reader may turn a prop about +y freely). A reader scales it uniformly by heightM / (bounds.max[1] - bounds.min[1]) and rests the point under its middle, (centre x, bounds.min[1], centre z), on the surface. The material is lit, not unlit: PBR metallic-roughness, base colour texture only, non-metal (metallicFactor 0), fully rough, single-sided; the mesh has no normals, so a reader computes them, and should draw both sides (the meshes are not reliably closed). The place's light (placeLight) is meant to fall on it

name.description: Unique within its place; the model's file name

description.description: What kind of thing it is and what it is made of

heightM.description: Its real height in metres, bottom to top

surface.description: What it rests on in a living room

bounds.description: The model's bounding box in its own units, [x, y, z]

placeLight.description: How the open place lights the reader's room, measured from its painted view (places.py light): a reader blends to it over the swap's fade in, and back over its fade out. Colours are light colours (brightest channel at full), sRGB

ambient.description: Light from above, around and below: the colours of the view's top, middle and bottom thirds (a trilight ambient)

key.description: The place's main light (its brightest region: a fire, lanterns, a lit window, the sun) as a directional light into the room. yaw and pitch are the direction from the seat toward the light, in the place's frame; the light shines back along it

yaw.description: Degrees about +y from the place's -z, its straight ahead (once placed: the direction from the seat to the key wall), positive toward +x, the right of a reader facing the key wall

strength.description: How much it stands out from the rest: near 0 for an evenly lit place, near 1 for a lamp in the dark

room.description: The grade of the reader's real room (on Quest, the passthrough's colour controls)

brightness.description: Change of the room's brightness: -0.4 is 40 % darker

occlusion.description: Contact-shadow and ambient-occlusion strength for the place's props: more for enclosed interiors

bbox.description: Normalised to the panel's full image size

id.description: Also the panel's folder name under panels/

size.description: Pixel size of the panel image; layer PNGs share it

depthScale.description: Metres of parallax spread between depth 0 and 1 at the default reading distance

strip.description: Where this panel sits on the original strip, in source pixels (episode.layout.width wide). Present for scroll layouts; the reader places the panel at y and leaves gutterAfter blank rows below it

durationOverride.description: Seconds; when absent the reader computes voices + 1.5 s per bubble, min 3 s, min 20 s for immersive modes, never below the longest animation. The pipeline writes it equal to endTime - startTime

startTime.description: Seconds from the episode's start when this panel becomes active, precomputed by the pipeline: one clock drives the episode, the panel whose [startTime, endTime) holds the clock is the active one, the ones after it have not played yet

endTime.description: Seconds from the episode's start when the next panel takes over; endTime - startTime is the panel's duration

frames.description: The comic frames inside the panel in reading order, precomputed by the pipeline: when each is reached (a reader shows the ones ahead greyed). A frame with balloons is reached at its first balloon; one without holds the clock for a fixed time. A frame is on screen from its start until the next frame of its panel starts, the last one until the panel ends

index.description: The frame's index in the panel's scene: the extras.frame of its nodes, a bubble's frame

setting.description: episode.settings[].id the frame is drawn in; absent for a frame with no place (a title, credits)

mood.description: Free text from the understanding pass; drives ambience and music prompts

layers.description: The panel's flat images: at least one when renderMode is panel. A panel with a scene carries none: the reader draws the scene alone

bubbles.description: In the order they appear on the clock

animations.description: What moves in the panel. The pipeline writes rule-based accents only (a pop, a cut, an impact: pipeline motion.py), each one track that plays once; what it writes, the reader shows

panorama.description: Equirectangular image, required when renderMode is panorama

scene.description: glb, required when renderMode is scene3d. A pipeline-made scene is the panel's layers as textured surfaces far to near, seen by its one camera (node panel_camera at the origin looking down -z; units are shares of the reading distance, the frames' windows at 1), unlit (KHR_materials_unlit), no texture over 2048 px on its long side. Every other node is one layer and says what it is in its glTF extras: kind (window, backdrop, character, object, lettering); frame (windows, and every layer shown through that frame's window: the reader clips those layers to the window's shape; lettering has none); card (every layer but the windows: its id in this panel, e.g. card-3, which bubbles[].speakerCard and animations[].target name); cast (a character that is a cast member: cast[].id); bubble (lettering: the id of its bubble in bubbles[], which the reader shows from that bubble's startTime)

name.description: Human label from segmentation, e.g. 'girl', 'lamp post'

image.description: RGBA PNG at panel size, holes behind it inpainted into the layer below

speakerId.description: cast[].id of who says it; absent when nobody the cast knows does (a caption, a sound effect, a voice from nowhere in the episode)

speakerCard.description: The card that says it: the extras.card of a node of this panel's scene (card-3), or <panelId>/<card> for a card drawn in another panel (p006/card-1: a voice carrying over from the box before or after; nothing in this panel to animate). Absent with a speakerId: that cast member speaks from off-panel. Absent without one: nobody speaks it

frame.description: The frame of the panel the bubble belongs to and is timed in (frames[].index, a node's extras.frame); absent in a panel without frames

kind.description: sfx: a sound no character voices, lettered on the art; never has audio or a speaker

anchor.description: Tail target, usually the speaker's mouth

anchorLayer.description: layer id the tail follows in parallax

audio.description: The line in its speaker's voice. Every bubble with a speakerCard and words has one in a pipeline-made file; a bubble without audio is shown for its durationHint as text only

durationHint.description: Seconds: the clip's length, or a reading time for a bubble without one

startTime.description: Seconds from the episode's start when the bubble appears and its clip starts, precomputed by the pipeline (= the panel's startTime + startOffset); a bubble whose startTime is ahead of the clock has not played yet

endTime.description: Seconds from the episode's start when the bubble's clip or reading time ends

animation.description: One track on one target. It starts at startTime on the episode clock (or delay seconds after its panel appears, the same moment) and runs for duration seconds; at local time u = (clock - start) / duration in 0..1 its value comes from keyframes (translate, rotate, scale, opacity) or from params (sway, shake, spriteCycle). Before its start a track does nothing. A track with loop false does nothing after its end either: the target is back at rest (the pipeline's tracks end at rest); with loop true it repeats. Tracks on one target combine: scales and opacities multiply, offsets and angles add. Offsets and scales act in the panel's plane (x to the right, y down, as panel pixels), never in depth

target.description: What moves. In a flat panel: a layer id. In a scene3d panel: a card (the node whose extras.card is this, e.g. card-3), or frame:<n> for the content of frame n: every node whose extras.frame is n except the frame's window, moved together behind the window, which stays still and clips them

startTime.description: Seconds from the episode's start (= the panel's startTime + delay). Present in pipeline-made files

loop.description: The pipeline always writes it; its accents are false

easing.description: How the value moves between two neighbouring keyframes, applied to each segment on its own share v of the way (0 at the earlier keyframe, 1 at the later): linear v; in v^3; out 1 - (1 - v)^3; inOut 4v^3 below a half, else 1 - (2 - 2v)^3 / 2; step: no glide, the earlier keyframe's value holds until the later keyframe's time (a cut)

pivot.description: rotate and scale: the fixed point, in the target's own bounding box as the panel camera sees it (0,0 its top-left, 1,1 its bottom-right). Default the centre; x 0.5, y 1 is the middle of its base

keyframes.description: For translate/rotate/scale/opacity: time 0..1 of the duration and a value, in time order; translate a vector in panel-normalised units (x a share of the panel's width, y of its height), rotate in degrees, scale a factor (1 = rest), opacity 0..1. Before the first keyframe its value holds, after the last its value holds

params.description: For sway/shake/spriteCycle. shake: an offset along axis of amplitude x (1 - u)^decay x sin(2 pi x frequency x d), d the seconds since the track started and u = d / duration; amplitude is a share of the panel's width, positive to the right

amplitude.description: sway, shake: the peak offset, panel-normalised

axis.description: shake: the direction of the offset

decay.description: shake: the exponent of (1 - u) the amplitude dies out by; 0 keeps it constant

pin.description: shake of a frame's content: cards (extras.card) that touch a side of the frame's window and must not be pulled away from it, since nothing is painted behind them there. A card pinned l takes only the offsets toward the left (negative) and stays at rest during the others; r only those toward the right; lr does not move
